subject: Privacy boundary clarification & next steps for FinTrust POC
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fintrust.io>, Jenna Park <jenna.park@fintrust.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Privacy boundary clarification & next steps for FinTrust POC

Alex / Jenna — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have alignment on the deployment-mode decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) and the data-isolation constraints that matter most to you.

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary need: strict tenant-level isolation for customer data + control over crypto keys (BYOK/KMS).
- Residency: all model inputs/outputs and logs must stay in US regions only.
- No multi-tenant GPU pools sharing customer data at rest or during inference.
- Auditability: access logs and retention controls for 12+ months, SOC2 evidence required.

Questions to help us recommend the best path (can you confirm the bold ones?):
1) Is BYOK required for production (customer-managed KMS), or is it acceptable for POC to use our managed keys with a transition plan to BYOK? (Please state: required / preferred / optional)
2) Do you require VPC peering (Private deployment) or would an isolated Dedicated pool (single-tenant GPU allocation within our infrastructure) satisfy the isolation requirement?
3) Any specific network egress restrictions or approved IP ranges we should know about?
4) Procurement timeline and any procurement-specific docs we should prepare (SOW, PO terms, security addendum)?

Next steps from Redwood:
- I'll coordinate with engineering for a short feasibility note comparing Dedicated (isolated tenant + BYOK on dedicated hardware) vs Private VPC (VPC peering or on-prem).
- Marissa will follow up with configuration and cost tradeoffs. Ben will draft an initial commercial outline for both paths.

Attachments: redwood_poc_checklist.pdf (POC checklist & required artifacts).

Available windows for a follow-up technical sync: Mon 12/7 10–11am PT or Tue 12/8 9–10am PT — what works for your team?

Thanks,
Hannah

Subject: Re: Privacy boundary clarification & next steps for FinTrust POC

Thanks Hannah — appreciate the summary. Quick answers inline and one clarification:

> 1) BYOK required for production?
For production: required. For POC: acceptable to use Redwood-managed keys for initial validation provided there9s a documented migration path to customer-managed KMS before we move to any production workloads.

> 2) VPC peering vs Dedicated pool?
We need VPC-level separation for network policy enforcement. The ideal is either: (a) Private VPC peering where our network team controls ingress/egress, or (b) an on-prem deployment if peering is not possible. A Dedicated pool that sits in Redwood-managed VPC is only acceptable if it can guarantee no shared control-plane access and support VPC-like controls for outbound filtering.

> 3) Egress restrictions / approved IPs
We have an approved outbound IP range list; procurement will share this. Also, traffic must not cross outside US regions.

> 4) Procurement timeline
We9re targeting an internal decision by end of year; procurement will need an SOW and a security addendum for BYOK/KMS responsibilities.

Attaching our Requirements doc for your engineering team: FinTrust_ACS_requirements.docx

—Alex

Date: Sat, 5 Dec 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Privacy boundary clarification & next steps for FinTrust POC

Hannah / Ben — quick draft outline attached (deployment_comparison_table.csv). TL;DR:
- Dedicated (isolated tenant) + BYOK: feasible. Implementation notes: provision a dedicated GPU pool, enable customer-managed KMS integration (we need ARNs and KMS admin access during onboarding), and apply region lockdown at tenancy level. Control-plane still runs in Redwood environment but we can provide strict RBAC and are willing to sign controls for no shared data access.
- Private VPC peering: highest isolation. Requires network team coordination (route tables, peering setup) and we9d need a maintenance window to configure. Slightly higher lead time and ops overhead.

Tradeoffs:
- Time to provision: Dedicated ~2–3 weeks (incl. KMS onboarding), Private VPC ~4–6 weeks depending on network approvals.
- Cost: Private VPC has additional setup fees and a higher monthly baseline; Dedicated is cheaper monthly but may not satisfy customers that require VPC-native controls.
- Auditability: both support logs and retention; for Private VPC we can push logs to customer SIEM.

I9ve attached a comparison CSV with columns: feature, Dedicated, Private VPC, notes. Ben, can you add a pricing sketch in that CSV and return today?

Attachments: deployment_comparison_table.csv

—Marissa

Subject: Next steps & two recommended paths — FinTrust POC

Alex / Jenna / Procurement team — thanks for the quick responses and patience while we mapped internal feasibility. Below is a short proposal with two viable paths and suggested next steps.

Option A — Dedicated isolated pool + BYOK (recommended near-term):
- What: single-tenant GPU pool provisioned for FinTrust, customer-managed KMS integration (we will require KMS ARNs and admin onboarding).
- Pros: faster to stand up (2–3 weeks), lower monthly baseline, supports our standard monitoring and SLOs.
- Cons: control-plane remains Redwood-hosted (we will provide strict RBAC & documented controls).

Option B — Private VPC peering / on-prem (highest isolation):
- What: VPC peering into FinTrust network or an on-prem package if peering is not acceptable.
- Pros: highest network-level isolation, logs can be pushed directly to your SIEM, meets strict network policy requirements.
- Cons: longer lead time (4–6 weeks), higher setup and baseline costs.

Requested from FinTrust to proceed with scoping: 
- Confirm whether POC may start under Option A using Redwood-managed keys with a firm commitment to move to BYOK before production.
- Share the outbound IP allowlist and KMS ARNs for provisioning.
- Confirm preferred follow-up time for technical onboarding: Tue 12/8 9–10am PT (engineering deep-dive) or Wed 12/9 11am–12pm PT.

I9ve attached two short overviews for your team: redwood_dedicated_config.pdf and redwood_private_overview.pdf. I9ll also open a HubSpot deal record and add the comparison table + our pricing sketch (link below).
